page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, featuring dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C hardware. The configuration provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 64 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2 GB per vCPU), and features an extensive 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets.

Storage provisions include 1888 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast ephemeral scratch disk performance alongside compatibility with Azure premium remote storage. No discrete graphics hardware is present on this virtual machine, reserving all thermal and compute allocation for host CPU calculations.

Benchmark results show notable strengths in compression, decompression, and text manipulation. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench text processing and small-model LLM text generation, while single-threaded gzip compression (35.44 GB/sec) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (202.24 GB/sec) test in the top quartile. Geekbench single-core (2191.0) and multi-core (17995.0) scores also reflect strong performance, whereas raw PassMark and stress-ng metrics fall within the middle 50% median.

By adopting a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile, the D32lds_v7 offers a cost-efficient hardware density for compute-bound tasks that do not require standard 1:4 memory allocation. The presence of fast local NVMe storage and hardware matrix extensions makes the instance technically suited for batch data processing, static web serving, software build clusters, and intermediate ETL staging.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. It features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 64 GB of system memory, and a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPU hardware. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration minimizes RAM allocation to favor compute efficiency. Empirical benchmarks place the instance in the top quartile for Geekbench multi-core operations, compression tasks, static web serving throughput, and small-model CPU-based LLM prompt processing. In addition, its support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions facilitates accelerated vector math. The combination of dense compute resources, fast local storage, and dedicated vCPUs makes the D32lds_v7 appropriate for CI/CD compilation, batch ETL pipelines, static web serving, and localized caching workloads.
